questions.question: Proper riding clothes offer all of the following, except:

options.text: Comfort.
Protection in a crash.
Protection from cold weather.
Discomfort.

questions.correctAnswerText: Discomfort.
questions.explanation: Proper riding clothes protect you from injury in a crash. They also protect you from weather and other hazards.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, you should:

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
Press the handle grip in the opposite direction of where you want to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then press the right to straighten. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: If a passing vehicle creates a wind blast that hits you, you will have the most room to recover if you are riding:

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane gives you the most room to recover if a wind blast affects your control.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They warn you about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: To carry a passenger, you may need to adjust all of the following, except:

options.text: Tire pressure.
Mirror positions.
Headlight position.
Brake light position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake light position.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle sits differently with a passenger due to extra weight. You may need to adjust tire pressure, suspension, headlight, and mirrors. The brake light position does not need adjustment.

questions.question: As weight shifts to the front of your bike while braking, you should:

options.text: Gradually increase pressure on the front brake.
Use more rear brake pressure.
Not worry about weight transfer.
Try to lock the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gradually increase pressure on the front brake.
questions.explanation: As you brake, gradually increase front brake pressure as the bike's weight moves forward to the front tire.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs that show speed limits are rectangular with white background and black lettering. You must follow these signs.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly while in a curve, you should:

options.text: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
Apply both brakes abruptly while leaning.
Apply only the rear brake.
Apply only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
questions.explanation: If you must stop quickly in a curve, first straighten the bike and square the handlebars, then stop. If you cannot straighten, apply brakes smoothly and gradually while reducing your lean angle.

questions.question: If the throttle gets stuck, you should:

options.text: Jump off the motorcycle.
Apply the brakes.
Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
Not touch the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
questions.explanation: If your throttle is stuck, twist it back and forth several times to free it. If that does not work, use the engine cut-off switch and pull the clutch in at the same time.

questions.question: A motorcyclist can prevent other vehicles from sharing their lane by:

options.text: Riding in the left portion of a lane.
Riding in the center portion of a lane.
Making gestures at other drivers.
Riding in a zigzag pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in the center portion of a lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to share your lane.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Ride more slowly than usual.
Start slowing down earlier than usual.
Increase your following distance.
Avoid talking to the passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid talking to the passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle, making it respond more slowly. You should ride slower, slow down earlier, and keep more distance behind other vehicles. Always warn your passenger about hazards ahead.

questions.question: If a dog chases your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Kick the dog away.
Ride alongside the dog.
Stop until the dog loses interest.
Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Downshift and approach the dog slowly. Then accelerate and leave it behind. If a larger animal chases you, brake and prepare to stop.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to drive, which action should you avoid?

options.text: Encourage other friends to talk them out of driving.
Arrange for other transportation.
Tell them to take less-crowded roads.
Slow their pace of drinking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell them to take less-crowded roads.
questions.explanation: You can help prevent drunk driving by arranging other transportation, keeping them busy to slow their drinking, using excuses to delay them leaving, and getting other friends involved to stop them together. Do not suggest safer driving routes instead of preventing them from driving.

questions.question: When planning a long group ride, which idea should you NOT use?

options.text: Plan travel segments based on the least experienced rider.
Skip breaks to reach your destination faster.
Place inexperienced riders behind the leaders.
Use a staggered riding formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Skip breaks to reach your destination faster.
questions.explanation: Plan trips and segments based on your least experienced rider. Take regular breaks to reduce tiredness. Place newer riders behind leaders so experienced riders can watch them. Ride in a staggered formation.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:

options.text: Happen at speeds greater than 35 mph.
Happen at night.
Are caused by worn tires.
Involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders who have been riding the same motorcycle for less than six months.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which instruction should you NOT give them?

options.text: Get on after the engine starts.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.
Hold firmly to your waist, hips, or belt.
Talk whenever they want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk whenever they want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should avoid talking or moving unnecessarily to help you focus on riding. They should board after the engine starts, sit forward without crowding you, and hold your waist, hips, or belt firmly.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes occur:

options.text: At speeds greater than 55 mph.
After several hours of riding.
On short trips.
On long trips.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles long at speeds slower than 30 mph.

questions.question: When it starts to rain while you are riding, you should:

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Increase your speed.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull onto the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane has oil buildup and becomes slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. Slow down on wet surfaces.

questions.question: The center portion of a lane:

options.text: Is always the best place for a motorcycle to ride.
Has oil and grease, but is usually safe for riding.
Has oil and grease, and is never safe for riding.
Is the smoothest part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has oil and grease, but is usually safe for riding.
questions.explanation: Oil drippings from cars build up in a strip down the center of lanes. Unless the road is wet, this area is usually safe for motorcycles. Avoid riding on heavy buildup of oil and grease, often found at busy intersections or toll booths.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: At high speeds.
After riding for a long time.
Far from home.
On short trips.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips less than five miles long at speeds slower than 30 mph.

questions.question: The middle of the lane usually has an oily strip. What should you do?

options.text: Avoid the oily strip when it is raining.
Ride only on the oily strip because it gives better grip.
Avoid the entire center of the lane.
Do not worry about oil or other things in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the oily strip when it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars and trucks collects in the center of each lane. When the road is dry, this strip usually has enough grip for a motorcycle. The strip is narrow enough that you can ride on either side and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: What should you do if your rear wheel locks while braking?

options.text: Release the brake until the tire grips again, then brake again.
Release the brake and use only the front brake.
Keep the brake locked until the motorcycle stops.
Release the brake and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the brake locked until the motorcycle stops.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while braking, do not release the brake. Keep it locked until you come to a complete stop.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time to a hazard?

options.text: Always ride below the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and both brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to a hazard.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve, not both.
Do not swerve and only use the front brake to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
questions.explanation: When you must brake and swerve, do these actions separately, not at the same time. Braking while swerving can cause your motorcycle to fall over.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for riding a motorcycle?

options.text: The left side of the lane
The center of the lane
The right side of the lane
The best position depends on your riding conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The best position depends on your riding conditions.
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best, and no position should always be avoided. Choose a position that fits your current riding conditions. Make sure you have enough space around you and that other drivers can see you.
